title.raw: 卷九十一 列傳第六十一 儒林 Volume 91 Biographies 61: Confucian Scholars

sentences.zh: 昔周德既衰，諸侯力政，禮經廢缺，雅頌陵夷。

translations.literal: In olden times the virtue of Zhou had already declined; the feudal lords wielded force in government; the ritual classics were cast aside and left incomplete; the Ya and Song sections of the Poetry sank into decay.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, as Zhou’s moral authority ebbed, the regional lords ruled by arms, the rites and their texts were neglected, and the high poetic tradition enshrined in the Odes fell away.

sentences.zh: 夫子將聖多能，固天攸縱，歎鳳鳥之不至，傷麟出之非時，於是乃刪《詩》《書》，定禮樂，贊《易》道，修《春秋》，載籍逸而復存，風雅變而還正。

translations.literal: The Master, near to sagehood and possessed of many abilities, was indeed what Heaven let run free; he sighed that the phoenix-bird did not come, and grieved that the unicorn appeared out of season; thereupon he edited the Poetry and the Documents, fixed the rites and music, elucidated the way of the Changes, and compiled the Spring and Autumn, so that written records, though scattered, were preserved again, and the Feng and Ya styles, though altered, were returned to correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, touched with sage-like gifts and versatile learning, was Heaven’s chosen instrument; he mourned the phoenix that never came and the untimely unicorn. He then shaped the Poetry and the Documents, set the rites and music to order, opened the meaning of the Changes, and gave final form to the Spring and Autumn—restoring what had been lost to the written tradition and bringing the literary styles of the Odes back to their proper standard.

sentences.zh: 其後卜商、衛賜、田、吳、孫、孟之儔，或親稟微言，或傳聞大義，猶能強晉存魯，籓魏卻秦，既抗禮於邦君，亦馳聲於海內。

translations.literal: Afterward followers such as Bu Shang, Wei Ci, and the likes of Tian, Wu, Sun, and Meng—some having personally received subtle teachings, others having heard transmitted great principles—were still able to strengthen Jin and preserve Lu, shield Wei and beat back Qin; they both stood on equal ceremonial footing with the lords of states and made their reputations resound within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Later disciples in the line of Zixia, Zigong, and others akin to the masters Tian, Wu, Sun, and Meng—whether they heard the Master’s subtle words firsthand or received his larger meanings at one remove—still performed feats such as shoring up Jin, saving Lu, protecting Wei, and turning back Qin; they faced regional rulers as peers in ritual and won fame across the realm.

sentences.zh: 及嬴氏慘虐，棄德任刑，煬墳籍於埃塵，填儒林於坑阱，嚴是古之法，抵挾書之罪，先王徽烈，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: When the house of Ying turned cruel and violent, casting aside virtue and relying on punishments, they burned the texts of tombs to ash and dust and filled the grove of Ru scholars with pits and traps; they made strict the laws against praising antiquity and punished the crime of concealing books; the glorious deeds of the former kings had not even a remnant left.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin tyranny, moral government was abandoned for harsh law; books were reduced to dust and scholars buried in execution pits; statutes condemned those who looked to the past, and owning a text became a crime—so that the legacy of the ancient kings was all but erased.

sentences.zh: 漢祖勃興，救焚拯溺，粗修禮律，未遑俎豆。

translations.literal: The Han founder rose with sudden vigor, rescuing the burned and the drowning; he roughly restored ritual and statutes, and had not yet leisure for the full refinements of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder seized power amid fire and flood, he patched together rites and laws, but there was as yet little room for the finer observances of the ancestral cult.

sentences.zh: 逮于孝武，崇尚文儒。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Xiaowu, literary learning and Ru scholarship were held in honor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han, letters and classical scholarship came into their own.

sentences.zh: 爰及東京，斯風不墜。

translations.literal: Reaching to Eastern Han, this wind did not fall away.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Later Han, that cultural momentum never quite died.

sentences.zh: 於是傍求蠹簡，博訪遺書，創甲乙之科，擢賢良之舉，莫不紆青拖紫，服冕乘軒，或徒步而取公卿，或累旬以膺臺鼎。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sought worm-eaten bamboo slips on every side and broadly inquired after lost writings; they instituted the jia and yi examination categories and raised up the "excellent and good" selections; none failed to trail purple sashes and wear vermilion seals, don caps of office and ride in high carriages—some attained the rank of duke or minister on foot, others in a few decades ascended to the highest councils.
translations.idiomatic: Courts then ransacked archives and hunted down stray texts, devised graded examinations and "worthy and good" recommendations; graduates wrapped themselves in high rank—some leapt from common status to the summit of the bureaucracy in a single bound, others climbed to chief minister within a few short years.

sentences.zh: 故縉紳之士，靡然向風，餘芳遺烈，煥乎可紀者也。

translations.literal: Therefore gentry in official sashes turned with the wind like grass; their lingering fragrance and surviving brilliance are splendid enough to record.
translations.idiomatic: Silk-girdled scholars flocked to the trend; what they left behind still shines brightly enough to merit remembrance.

sentences.zh: 洎當塗草創，深務兵權，而主好斯文，朝多君子，鴻儒碩學，無乏于時。

translations.literal: By the time the ruling house at Dangtu was first founded, they deeply applied themselves to military authority; yet the ruler loved this culture, the court held many gentlemen, and great Ru and eminent scholars were not lacking for the age.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei regime was still taking shape, power rested on the army, yet the sovereign cherished classical culture, the capital teemed with principled men, and first-rate scholars were never absent.

sentences.zh: 武帝受終，憂勞軍國，時既初並庸蜀，方事江湖，訓卒厲兵，務農積穀，猶復修立學校，臨幸辟雍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he worried and toiled over army and state; the times had only just annexed Yong and Shu, and he was still busy on the Yangzi and lakes, drilling troops and sharpening weapons, devoting effort to farming and stockpiling grain—yet he still established schools and personally visited the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin, inheriting the throne from Wei, bore the burdens of war and administration: Yongzhou and Bashu had only lately been subdued, and the lower Yangzi still demanded attention, so he trained soldiers, encouraged agriculture, and built granaries—even so, he founded schools and went in person to the ritual hall of learning.

sentences.zh: 而荀顗以制度贊惟新，鄭沖以儒宗登保傅，茂先以博物參朝政，子真以好禮居秩宗，雖愧明揚，亦非遐棄。

translations.literal: Yet Xun Yi, through institutions, assisted the renewal; Zheng Chong, as patriarch of Ru learning, rose to grand tutor; Maoxian (Zhang Hua), through encyclopedic knowledge, joined in court governance; Zi Zhen, through love of ritual, occupied the office of Minister of Rites—though they fell short of the ideal of transparent promotion, neither were they cast utterly aside.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi helped frame the new dynasty’s regulations; Zheng Chong, doyen of classical studies, became a tutor to the heir; Zhang Hua brought his wide learning into policy; the man known as Zi Zhen, esteemed for ritual, headed the cult of ancestors—they may not have been perfect choices, but they were hardly neglected talent.

sentences.zh: 既而荊揚底定，區寓乂安，群公草封禪之儀，天子發謙沖之詔，未足比靈斯三代，固亦擅美一時。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Jing and Yang were pacified and the realm was at peace, the high ministers drafted protocols for the Feng and Shan sacrifices, and the Son of Heaven issued modest edicts declining them—this was not enough to match the numinous virtue of the three dynasties, yet it still claimed a moment’s glory.
translations.idiomatic: Once the southeast was quiet and the empire rested easy, ministers drew up plans for the grand Feng and Shan offerings while the emperor answered with self-effacing refusals—far short of the sage-kings of antiquity, perhaps, but still a high-water mark for that age.

sentences.zh: 惠帝纘戎，朝昏政弛，釁起宮掖，禍成籓翰。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui took up the martial mantle; morning and evening governance slackened; provocation arose within the palace apartments, and disaster matured among the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui inherited a throne won by arms, yet day and night government grew lax; intrigue flared in the harem, and catastrophe brewed in the quarrels of the princely fiefs.

sentences.zh: 惟懷逮湣，喪亂弘多，衣冠禮樂，掃地俱盡。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperors Huai and Min, turmoil was vast indeed; caps and sashes, rites and music, were swept away together until nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: Through the reigns of Huai and Min, chaos spread without measure—courtly dress, ceremony, and music were utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 元帝運鐘百六，光啟中興，賀、荀、刁、杜諸賢並稽古博文，財成禮度。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan met the fate of the "hundred-six" calamity yet opened the renewal in the south; worthies such as He, Xun, Diao, and Du together investigated antiquity and broadened their literary learning, and helped complete the norms of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, though Heaven had decreed a time of disaster, launched the Eastern Jin restoration; He, Xun, Diao, Du, and others steeped themselves in the classics and letters, shaping the forms of public ritual.

sentences.zh: 雖尊儒勸學，亟降於綸言，東序西膠，未聞於弦誦。

translations.literal: Although honoring the Ru and encouraging study were repeatedly proclaimed in edicts, east hall and west school never echoed with the sound of recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial rhetoric still urged respect for scholars and the pursuit of learning, yet the schools stood largely silent—no steady hum of students at their texts.

sentences.zh: 明皇聰睿，雅愛流略，簡文玄嘿，敦悅丘墳，乃招集學徒，弘獎風烈，並時艱祚促，未能詳備。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was acute and wise, and had a refined love of bibliographic summaries; Emperor Jianwen was reserved and silent, yet delighted in the tombs of ancient texts; they gathered students of learning, encouraged high standards, but the times were hard and their reigns short, so nothing could be brought to full completion.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi loved books and catalogues; Jianwen, though retiring, cherished the classics; both summoned scholars and rewarded integrity, yet troubled times and brief reigns left their projects unfinished.

sentences.zh: 有晉始自中朝，迄于江左，莫不崇飾華競，祖述虛玄，擯闕里之典經，習正始之餘論，指禮法為流俗，目縱誕以清高，遂使憲章弛廢，名教頹毀，五胡乘間而競逐，二京繼踵以淪胥，運極道消，可為長歎息者矣。

translations.literal: From the central court down to the left bank of the Yangzi, none failed to adorn themselves in hollow brilliance and claim descent from empty profundity; they cast aside the canonical texts of the village of Confucius and practiced the leftover discourses of the Zhengshi era; they pointed to ritual and law as vulgar convention and looked on license and exaggeration as lofty purity—whereupon statutes grew lax, moral teaching collapsed, the five Hu peoples seized their opening and raced for power, and the two capitals fell one after the other into ruin; fate reached its limit and the Way waned—matter for a long, deep sigh.
translations.idiomatic: From Western Jin through the court-in-exile, fashion chased hollow brilliance and aped the abstruse talk of Zhengshi; the Analects and classics of Qufu were spurned while idle metaphysics flourished; ritual was mocked as pedestrian and wanton conduct praised as transcendence—so institutions rotted, ethical teaching failed, barbarian leaders poured through the breach, Luoyang and Chang’an fell in turn, and the age slid past recovery.

sentences.zh: 鄭沖等名位既隆，自有列傳，其餘編之于左，以續前史《儒林》云。

translations.literal: Zheng Chong and others, their fame and rank already lofty, have their own biographies; the rest are compiled here at left, to continue the former histories’ "Forest of Ru Scholars."
translations.idiomatic: Figures such as Zheng Chong, prominent enough to warrant separate chapters, appear elsewhere; those gathered here carry on the tradition of the "Ru Scholars" biographies of earlier dynastic histories.

sentences.zh: 范平

translations.literal: Fan Ping
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ping

sentences.zh: 范平，字子安，吳郡錢塘人也。

translations.literal: Fan Ping, styled Zi’an, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ping, courtesy Zi’an, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先銍侯馥，避王莽之亂適吳，因家焉。

translations.literal: His ancestor was Fu, Marquis of Zhi, who, fleeing the disorders of Wang Mang, went to Wu and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: His forebear was the Marquis of Zhi, Fu, who crossed south to Wu to escape Wang Mang’s upheaval and settled there.

sentences.zh: 平研覽墳素，遍該百氏，姚信、賀邵之徒皆從受業。

translations.literal: Ping studied and perused the ancient plain texts and mastered the teachings of the hundred schools; men such as Yao Xin and He Shao all took instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ping pored over classical texts until he commanded the major schools of thought; scholars like Yao Xin and He Shao studied under him.

sentences.zh: 吳時舉茂才，累遷臨海太守，政有異能。

translations.literal: In Wu times he was recommended as maocai and was promoted step by step to governor of Linhai, where his administration showed unusual ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under Eastern Wu he rose on a maocai recommendation to governor of Linhai, where his rule was conspicuously effective.

sentences.zh: 孫皓初，謝病還家，敦悅儒學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sun Hao’s reign he pleaded illness and returned home, devoting himself wholeheartedly to Ru learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao took the throne, Fan claimed ill health, retired, and immersed himself in classical studies.

sentences.zh: 吳平，太康中，頻征不起，年六十九卒。

translations.literal: After Wu fell, in the Taikang years he was summoned repeatedly but would not go; he died at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu surrendered, the court called for him repeatedly during the Taikang era, but he refused every summons; he died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 有詔追加諡號曰文貞先生，賀循勒碑紀其德行。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously added the posthumous title "Wenzhen," Gentleman Wen, and He Xun composed an inscription praising his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him the posthumous name Wenzhen, and He Xun had a stele carved celebrating his character.

sentences.zh: 三子：奭、咸、泉，並以儒學至大官。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Shi, Xian, and Quan; all rose to high office on the strength of classical scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons—Shi, Xian, and Quan—each climbed to senior rank through scholarly reputation.

sentences.zh: 泉子蔚，關內侯。

translations.literal: Quan’s son Wei was a marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Quan’s son Wei held the title of marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 家世好學，有書七千餘卷。

translations.literal: For generations the family loved learning and owned more than seven thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The household had long cherished books and kept a library of over seven thousand fascicles.

sentences.zh: 遠近來讀者恆有百餘人，蔚為辦衣食。

translations.literal: Those who came from near and far to read were constantly over a hundred in number, and Wei provided them food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred readers habitually gathered from the region; Wei supplied their board and lodging.

sentences.zh: 蔚子文才，亦幼知名。

translations.literal: Wei’s son Wencai was also known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s son Wencai won notice while still a boy.

sentences.zh: 文立

translations.literal: Wen Li
translations.idiomatic: Wen Li

sentences.zh: 文立，字廣休，巴郡臨江人也。

translations.literal: Wen Li, styled Guangxiu, was a man of Linjiang in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Li, courtesy Guangxiu, hailed from Linjiang in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 蜀時遊太學，專《毛詩》、《三禮》，師事譙周，門人以立為顏回，陳壽、李虔為游夏，羅憲為子貢。

translations.literal: In Shu-Han times he studied at the Imperial Academy, specializing in the Mao version of the Poetry and the three ritual texts; he studied under Qiao Zhou, and among his fellow students the school took Li as its Yan Hui, Chen Shou and Li Qian as its Ziyou and Zixia, and Luo Xian as its Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shu he attended the Imperial Academy, focusing on the Mao Poetry and the three Rites, with Qiao Zhou as his teacher; classmates likened him to Yan Hui, paired Chen Shou and Li Qian with Ziyou and Zixia, and compared Luo Xian to Zigong.

sentences.zh: 仕至尚書。

translations.literal: He served until he reached the post of imperial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His official career culminated in the position of imperial secretary.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，舉秀才，除郎中。

translations.literal: When Shu fell he was recommended as xiucai and appointed gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Shu he earned a xiucai nomination and became a palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，拜濟陰太守，入為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was appointed governor of Jiyin and then entered court as junior tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era he became governor of Jiyin, then returned to the capital as junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上表請以諸葛亮、蔣琬、費禕等子孫流徙中畿，宜見敘用，一以慰巴蜀之心，其次傾吳人之望，事皆施行。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking that the descendants of Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and others, who had been relocated to the central plain, ought to be reviewed and employed—first to reassure the hearts of Ba and Shu, second to sway the expectations of the people of Wu; the matter was implemented in every case.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned that the exiled descendants of Shu luminaries such as Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, and Fei Yi be found posts—partly to console former Shu subjects, partly to win goodwill in Wu—and the throne approved each recommendation.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太子中庶子文立忠貞清實，有思理器幹。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The junior tutor to the heir apparent, Wen Li, is loyal, pure, and solid, possessed of reflective judgment and practical capacity.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Junior Tutor Wen Li is steadfast, honest, and capable, with a clear mind for affairs."

sentences.zh: 前濟在陰，政事修明。

translations.literal: When previously in Jiyin, administrative affairs were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In his earlier tenure at Jiyin he governed with conspicuous competence.

sentences.zh: 後事東宮，盡輔導之節。

translations.literal: Later, serving the Eastern Palace, he fulfilled every duty of instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: At the heir’s residence he carried out the full responsibilities of a tutor.

sentences.zh: 昔光武平隴蜀，皆收其賢才以敘之，蓋所以拔幽滯而濟殊方也。

translations.literal: In olden days Guangwu, having pacified Long and Shu, gathered their worthy men and employed them—by this means he raised the submerged and aided distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Guangwu, after conquering Long and Shu, enrolled their best men to office—precisely to lift the obscure and strengthen the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 其以立為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Let Li be appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Li cavalier attendant-in-ordinary."

sentences.zh: 」蜀故尚書犍為程瓊雅有德業，與立深交。

translations.literal: " Cheng Qiong of Qianwei, the former imperial secretary of Shu, was a man of refined virtue and achievement, and was on close terms with Li.
translations.idiomatic: The edict continued: Cheng Qiong of Qianwei, Shu’s former imperial secretary, was a man of sterling character and Li’s intimate friend.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞其名，以問立，對曰：「臣至知其人，但年垂八十，稟姓謙退，無復當時之望，不以上聞耳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu heard his name he asked Li about him; Li replied, "Your servant knows the man well, but he is nearly eighty, of a retiring and modest nature, and no longer commands the reputation he once had; therefore I have not reported him upward."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, hearing Cheng’s name, questioned Li, who answered, "I know him intimately, but he is almost eighty, modest and withdrawn, and past the age when men expect preferment—so I never brought him to Your Majesty’s attention."

sentences.zh: 」瓊聞之曰：「廣休可謂不黨矣，故吾善夫人也。

translations.literal: When Qiong heard this he said, "Guangxiu may truly be called free of faction; therefore I have always esteemed him."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qiong remarked, "Guangxiu is proof that one can be fair-minded—that is why I have always respected him."

sentences.zh: 」時西域獻馬，帝問立：「馬何如？

translations.literal: At that time the Western Regions presented horses, and the emperor asked Li, "How are the horses?"
translations.idiomatic: When tribute horses arrived from the Western Regions, the sovereign asked Wen Li, "What do you make of these horses?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「乞問太僕。

translations.literal: He replied, "I beg to refer the matter to the grand groom."
translations.idiomatic: Li answered, "You should put that question to the grand groom."

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his discretion.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commandant of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 咸寧末，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianning he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died toward the end of the Xianning era.

sentences.zh: 所著章奏詩賦數十篇行於世。

translations.literal: His memorials, poems, and rhapsodies, several tens of pieces in all, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of his memorials, poems, and fu survive in circulation.

sentences.zh: 陳邵

translations.literal: Chen Shao
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shao

sentences.zh: 陳邵，字節良，東海襄賁人也。

translations.literal: Chen Shao, styled Jieliang, was a man of Xiangben in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shao, courtesy Jieliang, came from Xiangben in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，不就。

translations.literal: The commandery nominated him as filial and incorrupt, but he did not take up office.
translations.idiomatic: The local administration recommended him as filial and incorrupt, yet he declined appointment.

sentences.zh: 以儒學徵為陳留內史，累遷燕王師。

translations.literal: He was summoned on account of classical learning and made interior secretary of Chenliu, then rose in stages to tutor to the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Classical scholarship brought him a summons to interior secretary of Chenliu, after which he climbed to tutor to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 撰《周禮評》，甚有條貫，行於世。

translations.literal: He composed a Commentary on the Zhou Rites that was very systematic and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Zhou Rites Commentary was tightly organized and widely read.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，詔曰：「燕王師陳邵清貞潔靜，行著邦族，篤志好古，博通六籍，耽悅典誥，老而不倦，宜在左右以篤儒教。

translations.literal: In the Taishi years an edict said: "The tutor to the Prince of Yan, Chen Shao, is pure, upright, and quiet; his conduct is renowned in his clan; he is steadfast in purpose, loves antiquity, thoroughly masters the six classics, delights in canonical pronouncements, and in old age is not weary; he should attend at court to deepen Ru instruction.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi an edict declared: Chen Shao, tutor to the Prince of Yan, is chaste, retiring, and noted in his lineage; devoted to antiquity and fluent in the six classics, he still burns with scholarly zeal in age—keep him at court to strengthen Confucian teaching.

sentences.zh: 可為給事中。

translations.literal: He may serve as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Let him take office as palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 」卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while holding the post.

sentences.zh: 虞喜

translations.literal: Yu Xi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi

sentences.zh: 虞喜，字仲寧，會稽余姚人，光祿潭之族也。

translations.literal: Yu Xi, styled Zhongning, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji, of the same clan as the Guangluxun Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi, courtesy Zhongning, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji and belonged to the lineage of Guangluxun Yu Tan.

sentences.zh: 父察，吳征虜將軍。

translations.literal: His father Cha was general who campaigns against invaders for Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cha had been Wu’s general who campaigns against invaders.

sentences.zh: 喜少立操行，博學好古。

translations.literal: From youth Xi established conduct and integrity; he was broadly learned and loved antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi formed his character early, combining wide learning with a passion for the past.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恢臨郡，屈為功曹。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Hui came as governor of the commandery, Xi was pressed into service as merit assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui, on becoming governor, conscripted him as merit assessor.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，州舉秀才，司徒辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: He was inspected as filial and incorrupt, the province raised him as xiucai, and the minister of education summoned him, but in each case he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Filial-and-incorrupt nomination, provincial xiucai selection, and summons from the minister of education all came his way; he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 元帝初鎮江左，上疏薦喜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan first held the left Yangzi region, he submitted a memorial recommending Xi.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Emperor Yuan secured the southeast, he memorialized to recommend Yu Xi.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，公車徵拜博士，不就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended the throne, the imperial carriage office summoned him as erudite, but he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai’s accession brought a summons to the erudite chair; Xi stayed home.

sentences.zh: 喜邑人賀循為司空，先達貴顯，每詣喜，信宿忘歸，自云不能測也。

translations.literal: Xi’s townsman He Xun became minister of works, eminent and exalted; whenever he visited Xi he would lodge overnight and forget to return, saying of himself that he could not fathom Xi’s depth.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun of his own county, already a powerful minister, would visit and linger for days, confessing that he could not plumb Xi’s mind.

sentences.zh: 太寧中，與臨海任旭俱以博士徵，不就。

translations.literal: In the Taining years he and Ren Xu of Linhai were both summoned as erudites, but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: During Taining he and Ren Xu of Linhai were jointly summoned as erudites; both declined.

sentences.zh: 復下詔曰：「夫興化致政，莫尚乎崇道教，明退素也。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "In transforming customs and perfecting government, nothing surpasses honoring the teachings of the Way and clarifying retirement and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: A follow-up edict declared: "To improve morals and administration, nothing tops promoting the Way and honoring quiet integrity.

sentences.zh: 喪亂以來，儒雅陵夷，每覽《子衿》之詩，未嘗不慨然。

translations.literal: Since the disasters of rebellion, Ru elegance has declined; whenever I peruse the poem 'Zi Jin,' I cannot but sigh with feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars, classical culture has withered; each time I read the 'Zi Jin' ode, I am moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 臨海任旭、會稽虞喜並潔靜其操，歲寒不移，研精墳典，居今行古，志操足以勵俗，博學足以明道，前雖不至，其更以博士徵之。

translations.literal: Ren Xu of Linhai and Yu Xi of Kuaiji alike keep their conduct pure and quiet, unchanging through the years’ cold; they delve into the tombs and canons, dwelling in the present yet walking the ways of antiquity; their resolve is enough to reform vulgar habits, their learning enough to illuminate the Way; though they did not come before, let them again be summoned as erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xu and Yu Xi maintain spotless lives and unwavering resolve, mine the classics, live in the present yet embody ancient virtue, and possess both the character to shame the mediocre and the knowledge to clarify principle; summon them once more as erudites even though they stayed away the first time.

sentences.zh: 」喜辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: Xi pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Xi pleaded illness and again refused.

sentences.zh: 咸和末，詔公卿舉賢良方正直言之士，太常華恆舉喜為賢良。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianhe an edict ordered dukes and ministers to recommend worthy, good, and outspoken men; the minister of sacrifices Hua Heng nominated Xi as worthy and good.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xianhe the court called for candid men of talent; Hua Heng, minister of sacrifices, put forward Yu Xi as worthy and good.

sentences.zh: 會國有軍事，不行。

translations.literal: Because the state had military affairs, it did not take effect.
translations.idiomatic: Wartime needs prevented the appointment.

sentences.zh: 咸康初，內史何充上疏曰：「臣聞二八舉而四門穆，十亂用而天下安，徽猷克闡，有自來矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiankang the interior secretary He Chong submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that when the Eight Elders were raised the four gates were tranquil, and when the Ten Disordered ministers were employed the realm was at peace—brilliant plans have opened the way from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiankang Interior Secretary He Chong wrote: "I am told that when Shun chose eight men the four approaches grew still, and when the Zhou kings used the 'ten disordered' ministers the world found peace—such enlightened measures reach deep into antiquity.

sentences.zh: 方今聖德欽明，思恢遐烈，旌輿整駕，俟賢而動。

translations.literal: Now sagely virtue is bright and thoughtful, and you aim to restore far-reaching glory; the imperial carriage is harnessed, waiting for worthies before it moves.
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty’s virtue is luminous and your mind set on reviving great deeds; the court stands ready, chariots hitched, until worthy men appear.

sentences.zh: 伏見前賢良虞喜天挺貞素，高尚邈世，束脩立德，皓首不倦，加以傍綜廣深，博聞強識，鑽堅研微有弗及之勤，處靜味道無風塵之志，高枕柴門，怡然自足。

translations.literal: I have observed that the former worthy-and-good nominee Yu Xi is naturally upright and plain, lofty and detached from the age; he cultivates virtue with the bundle of silks [of a student] and in hoary age never tires; moreover he ranges broadly and deeply, remembers all he reads, drills into hard problems with tireless zeal, dwells in stillness and savors the Way without ambition for the dust of office, pillows his head on a brushwood gate and is content in himself.
translations.idiomatic: The former nominee Yu Xi is by nature honest and retiring, aloof from vulgar ambition; he has pursued learning from youth to white hair, commands vast erudition, probes the subtlest questions, prefers reclusion to career, and finds peace behind a humble gate.

sentences.zh: 宜使蒲輪紆衡，以旌殊操，一則翼贊大化，二則敦勵薄俗。

translations.literal: He should be brought in a cushioned carriage with jade fittings, to signal extraordinary conduct—on the one hand assisting great transformation, on the other encouraging a thin-spirited age.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch the honor carriage of state to mark his uniqueness—both to aid your grand civilizing project and to shame a shallow generation into better conduct.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，詔曰：「尋陽翟湯、會稽虞喜並守道清貞，不營世務，耽學高尚，操擬古人。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, an edict said: "Di Tang of Xunyang and Yu Xi of Kuaiji alike keep the Way pure and chaste, do not traffic with worldly affairs, devote themselves to study, and hold conduct modeled on the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: Di Tang of Xunyang and Yu Xi of Kuaiji both cleave to a spotless path, shun worldly entanglements, love learning, and model themselves on antiquity.

sentences.zh: 往雖徵命而不降屈，豈素絲難染而搜引禮簡乎！

translations.literal: Though in the past summons came and they did not bend—is it that plain silk cannot be dyed, or that our ritual overtures were too cursory?
translations.idiomatic: Though earlier calls failed to move them, is it because integrity cannot be bought, or because our invitations lacked proper respect?

sentences.zh: 政道須賢，宜納諸廊廟，其並以散騎常侍徵之。

translations.literal: Government needs worthies; they should be brought into the halls of state; let both be summoned as cavaliers attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The realm requires such men; install them at court—summon both as cavaliers attendant-in-ordinary."

sentences.zh: 」又不起。

translations.literal: Again they did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Again they stayed away.

sentences.zh: 永和初，有司奏稱十月殷祭，京兆府君當遷祧室，征西、豫章、潁川三府君初毀主，內外博議不能決。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghe the responsible office reported that in the tenth month’s Yin sacrifice the spirit tablet of the metropolitan prefect ought to move to the distant temple, while the spirit tablets of the three prefects—general who guards the west, of Yuzhang, and of Yingchuan—were newly subject to destruction, and broad discussion inside and outside could not settle it.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yonghe officials noted that for the autumn Yin offering the tablet of the metropolitan ancestor should shift to the remote shrine while new "destruction" rules applied to three lineage tablets; court and countryside debated without resolution.

sentences.zh: 時喜在會稽，朝廷遣就喜諮訪焉。

translations.literal: At that time Xi was in Kuaiji, and the court sent envoys to consult him on the point.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi was then in Kuaiji, and the government dispatched officers to seek his judgment.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus he was esteemed to such a degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight the court placed on his opinion.

sentences.zh: 喜專心經傳，兼覽讖緯，乃著《安天論》以難渾、蓋，又釋《毛詩略》，注《孝經》，為《志林》三十篇。

translations.literal: Xi devoted himself to the classics and commentaries, also perusing prognostication texts; thereupon he wrote the Treatise Securing Heaven to challenge the armillary-sphere and umbrella hypotheses, again explained the Mao Poetry in brief, annotated the Classic of Filial Piety, and composed thirty chapters of Records of Intent.
translations.idiomatic: He concentrated on the classics and apocrypha, wrote the Treatise Securing Heaven to debate cosmological models, produced a short exegesis of the Mao Poetry, a commentary on the Filial Piety, and thirty chapters of the Records of Intent.

sentences.zh: 凡所注述數十萬言，行於世。

translations.literal: In all, his annotated writings ran to several hundred thousand characters and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarly works totaled several hundred thousand graphs and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 年七十六卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-six without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-six, leaving no male heir.

sentences.zh: 弟豫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yu is treated in another chapter.

sentences.zh: 劉兆

translations.literal: Liu Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao

sentences.zh: 劉兆，字延世，濟南東平人，漢廣川惠王之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhao, styled Yanshi, was a man of Dongping in Jinan, a descendant of Prince Hui of Guangchuan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao, courtesy Yanshi, hailed from Dongping in Jinan commandery and traced descent from Han’s Prince Hui of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 兆博學洽聞，溫篤善誘，從受業者數千人。

translations.literal: Zhao was broadly learned and well informed, warm and earnest and skilled at teaching; those who received instruction from him numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao combined encyclopedic knowledge with a gentle, inspiring manner; thousands sat at his feet.

sentences.zh: 武帝時五辟公府，三征博士，皆不就。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu he was summoned five times to the three ducal offices and three times as erudite, but never took office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu summoned him five times to high ministerial posts and thrice to an erudite chair; he declined every time.

sentences.zh: 安貧樂道，潛心著述，不出門庭數十年。

translations.literal: Content with poverty and devoted to the Way, he immersed himself in writing and for several decades did not step beyond his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He embraced poverty for the sake of learning, wrote without cease, and rarely left home for decades.

sentences.zh: 以《春秋》一經而三家殊塗，諸儒是非之議紛然，互為仇敵，乃思三家之異，合而通之。

translations.literal: Because the single classic Spring and Autumn had three schools with divergent paths, and the various Ru wrangled over right and wrong until they became mutual enemies, he pondered the differences of the three houses and united them in comprehension.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn existed in three rival traditions whose partisans attacked one another; Liu Zhao studied their disagreements and sought a synthesis.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》有調人之官，作《春秋調人》七萬餘言，皆論其首尾，使大義無乖，時有不合者，舉其長短以通之。

translations.literal: The Zhou Rites contains the office of harmonizer among the people; he composed the Spring and Autumn Harmonizer in more than seventy thousand words, discussing beginning and end throughout so that the great meaning would not contradict itself; where there were points that still did not agree, he set forth the strengths and weaknesses to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhou Rites names a "harmonizer" for public disputes, he wrote the Spring and Autumn Harmonizer—over seventy thousand characters tracing each passage so the overarching message cohered, smoothing residual conflicts by weighing rival readings.

sentences.zh: 又為《春秋左氏》解，名曰《全綜》，《公羊》、《谷梁》，解詁皆納經傳中，硃書以別之。

translations.literal: He also composed an exegesis of Zuo’s tradition of the Spring and Autumn, calling it Comprehensive Synthesis; for the Gongyang and Guliang traditions, he embedded the glosses within the classic and commentary, using vermilion ink to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: He also produced a commentary on the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn under the title Comprehensive Synthesis, weaving Gongyang and Guliang glosses into the text of the classic and its commentaries and marking them in red for clarity.

sentences.zh: 又撰《周易訓注》，以正動二體互通其文。

translations.literal: He further compiled Exegetical Notes on the Zhou Changes, using the two trigram bodies of quiescence and movement to mutually clarify their wording.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a training commentary on the Book of Changes that correlated the static and dynamic aspects of the hexagrams to explain their lines.

sentences.zh: 凡所贊述百餘萬言。

translations.literal: In all, the works he composed and elucidated exceeded a million characters.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarly writings altogether ran to more than a million graphs.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人著靴騎驢至兆門外，曰：「吾欲見劉延世。

translations.literal: Once a man wearing boots rode a donkey to Zhao’s gate and said, "I wish to see Liu Yanshi."
translations.idiomatic: Someone once rode up to Liu Zhao’s door in boots on a donkey, announcing that he wanted an audience with Liu Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 」兆儒德道素，青州無稱其字者，門人大怒。

translations.literal: Zhao’s Ru virtue and daily conduct were plain and unadorned; in Qingzhou no one called him by his courtesy name, and his disciples were greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao’s scholarly character was modest and retiring—so much so that people in Qingzhou never used his polite name—and his students took deep offense at the visitor’s bluntness.

sentences.zh: 兆曰：「聽前。

translations.literal: Zhao said, "Let him come forward."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao said, "Show him in."

sentences.zh: 」既進，踞床問兆曰：「聞君大學，比何所作？

translations.literal: When he had entered, he sat sprawling on the couch and asked Zhao, "I hear you are greatly learned—what have you been working on lately?"
translations.idiomatic: The man came in, lounged on a seat, and demanded, "They say you are a great scholar—what is it you actually do?"

sentences.zh: 」兆答如上事，末云：「多有所疑。

translations.literal: Zhao answered with the matters above, and at the end said, "There is much of which I remain doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao outlined his projects and added that many points still puzzled him.

sentences.zh: 」客問之。

translations.literal: The guest asked about them.
translations.idiomatic: The stranger pressed him on those doubts.

sentences.zh: 兆說疑畢，客曰：「此易解耳。

translations.literal: When Zhao had finished explaining his doubts, the guest said, "These are easy to resolve."
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zhao had laid out every question, the visitor replied, "That is all quite simple."

sentences.zh: 」因為辯釋疑者是非耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he debated and explained which points of doubt were right or wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He then walked through each crux and showed which readings held up and which did not.

sentences.zh: 兆別更立意，客一難，兆不能對。

translations.literal: Zhao shifted to a new line of argument; the guest posed one objection, and Zhao could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao tried a fresh approach; the visitor countered once, and Zhao had no reply.

sentences.zh: 客去，已出門，兆欲留之，使人重呼還。

translations.literal: When the guest had gone, already outside the gate, Zhao wished to detain him and sent someone urgently to call him back.
translations.idiomatic: As the man was leaving, Liu Zhao thought better of letting him go and sent servants to hurry him back.

sentences.zh: 客曰：「親親在此營葬，宜赴之，後當更來也。

translations.literal: The guest said, "A kinsman here is arranging a funeral—I ought to attend; I shall come another time."
translations.idiomatic: The stranger answered, "I must bury a relative nearby; I will return another day."

sentences.zh: 」既去，兆令人視葬家，不見此客，竟不知姓名。

translations.literal: After he left, Zhao had people watch the funeral house; they did not see this guest, and in the end his name was never known.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao sent men to the supposed funeral site, but no such guest appeared; his identity remained a mystery.

sentences.zh: 兆年六十六卒。

translations.literal: Zhao died at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 有五子：卓、炤、耀、育、臍。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Zhuo, Zhao, Yao, Yu, and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He left five sons: Zhuo, Zhao, Yao, Yu, and Qi.

sentences.zh: 氾毓

translations.literal: Fan Yu
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yu

sentences.zh: 氾毓，字稚春，濟北盧人也。

translations.literal: Fan Yu, styled Zhichun, was a man of Lu in northern Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yu, courtesy Zhichun, came from Lu in northern Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 奕世儒素，敦睦九族，客居青州，逮毓七世，時人號其家「兒無常父，衣無常主，」毓少履高操，安貧有志業。

translations.literal: For generations the family had been Ru scholars of plain living; they treated the nine agnatic branches with generous harmony; dwelling as guests in Qingzhou, down to Yu’s generation it was seven generations; people of the time called their household "sons without a fixed father, garments without a fixed master." Yu in youth practiced lofty conduct, was content with poverty, and had determined aims.
translations.idiomatic: The clan had long been devoted to classical learning and mutual care among kinsmen; resident in Qingzhou for seven generations, outsiders said of them that no child lacked a father figure and no robe lacked an owner—such was their communal charity. Fan Yu, still young, embraced high standards, accepted want, and cherished clear goals.

sentences.zh: 父終，居於墓所三十餘載，至晦朔，躬掃墳壟，循行封樹，還家則不出門庭。

translations.literal: When his father died, he dwelt at the tomb site for more than thirty years; at each new and full moon he personally swept the mounds and walked the boundary trees; when he returned home he did not step beyond the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: After his father’s death he lived beside the grave for over thirty years, sweeping the burial mounds himself at every month’s beginning and midpoint, and on returning home he never left the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 或薦之武帝，召補南陽王文學、秘書郎、太傅參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: Someone recommended him to Emperor Wu, who summoned him to fill the posts of literary instructor to the Prince of Nanyang, secretary gentleman, and staff adviser to the grand tutor, but in no case would he accept.
translations.idiomatic: The throne called him to serve as tutor in letters to the Prince of Nanyang, palace secretary, and adviser to the grand tutor; he refused every appointment.

sentences.zh: 于時青土隱逸之士劉兆、徐苗等皆務教授，惟毓不蓄門人，清靜自守。

translations.literal: At that time among recluses of Qingzhou such as Liu Zhao and Xu Miao all engaged in teaching, but only Yu kept no private disciples and preserved purity and quiet in self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Other Qingzhou hermits like Liu Zhao and Xu Miao ran schools, whereas Fan Yu took no formal students and lived in studious seclusion.

sentences.zh: 時有好古慕德者諮詢，亦傾懷開誘，以一隅示之。

translations.literal: When men who loved antiquity and admired virtue came for counsel, he likewise opened his heart and guided them, showing them a corner of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when sincere seekers knocked, he shared his mind freely and pointed them toward the right path.

sentences.zh: 合《三傳》為之解注，撰《春秋釋疑》、《肉刑論》，凡是述造七萬餘言。

translations.literal: He combined the Three Traditions into a single commentary and exegesis, composed Spring and Autumn Doubts Dispelled and Discourse on Corporal Punishment—in all, somewhat more than seventy thousand characters of original writing.
translations.idiomatic: He merged the three Spring and Autumn commentaries into one annotated edition, wrote Spring and Autumn Doubts Dispelled and a treatise On Corporal Punishment, and produced over seventy thousand characters of scholarship.

sentences.zh: 年七十一卒。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 徐苗

translations.literal: Xu Miao
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao

sentences.zh: 徐苗，字叔胄，高密淳於人也。

translations.literal: Xu Miao, styled Shuzhou, was a man of Chunyu in Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, courtesy Shuzhou, hailed from Chunyu in Gaomi commandery.

sentences.zh: 累世相承，皆以博士為郡守。

translations.literal: Generation after generation they succeeded one another, all serving as erudites who became governors of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had produced classical scholars who went on to govern commanderies as erudite officials.

sentences.zh: 曾祖華，有至行。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hua possessed the utmost conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Hua was a man of consummate virtue.

sentences.zh: 嘗宿亭舍，夜有神人告之「亭欲崩」，遽出，得免。

translations.literal: Once he lodged at a post station; in the night a spirit person told him, "The station is about to collapse"; he rushed out and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: While staying at a courier inn he was warned in a dream that the roof would fall; he fled and survived.

sentences.zh: 祖邵，為魏尚書郎，以廉直見稱。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was a gentleman of the masters of writing for Wei and was praised for integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao had been a Wei court secretary renowned for honesty and bluntness.

sentences.zh: 苗少家貧，晝執鋤耒，夜則吟誦。

translations.literal: Miao in youth was poor at home; by day he wielded hoe and plow, by night he recited texts.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was destitute, farming by daylight and chanting classics after dark.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，與弟賈就博士濟南宋鈞受業，遂為儒宗。

translations.literal: At the capping age he went with his younger brother Jia to study under the erudite Song Jun of southern Ji, and thereupon became a patriarch of Ru learning.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he and his brother Jia studied under the erudite Song Jun in southern Ji and emerged as a leading Confucian voice.

sentences.zh: 作《五經同異評》，又依道家著《玄微論》，前後所造數萬言，皆有義味。

translations.literal: He wrote Evaluations of Agreements and Differences in the Five Classics, and following Daoist lines composed Subtle Treatise on the Dark; in all, several tens of thousands of characters produced before and after, each piece rich in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He authored a comparative study of the five classics and, in a Daoist vein, the Subtle Treatise on the Dark—tens of thousands of thoughtful characters in all.

sentences.zh: 性抗烈，輕財貴義，兼有知人之鑒。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and ardent, slighting wealth and honoring righteousness, and he also possessed the discernment to know men.
translations.idiomatic: He was fiery and principled, scorned riches, prized duty, and could read character shrewdly.

sentences.zh: 弟患口癰，膿潰，苗為吮之。

translations.literal: His younger brother suffered a mouth abscess that festered; Miao sucked the wound for him.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother’s mouth ulcer suppurated, Xu Miao drew out the poison with his mouth.

sentences.zh: 其兄弟皆早亡，撫養孤遺，慈愛聞於州里，田宅奴婢盡推與之。

translations.literal: His brothers all died young; he raised the orphaned children with kindness famed in the district, and turned over to them every field, house, and slave.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers died early; he reared their children and gave them every scrap of property, winning countywide renown for compassion.

sentences.zh: 鄉鄰有死者，便輟耕助營棺槨，門生亡于家，即斂於講堂。

translations.literal: When a neighbor died he would stop plowing to help supply a coffin; when a disciple died at home he laid the body out in his lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: He halted farming to help neighbors bury their dead, and embalmed a student who died on his premises in the school hall.

sentences.zh: 其行己純至，類皆如此。

translations.literal: In conducting himself he was pure and thorough; his deeds were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such unstinting integrity marked everything he did.

sentences.zh: 遠近咸歸其義，師其行焉。

translations.literal: Near and far submitted to his righteousness and modeled their conduct on his.
translations.idiomatic: People from every quarter honored his example and copied his ways.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，州辟從事、治中、別駕、舉異行，公府五辟博士，再徵，並不就。

translations.literal: The commandery inspected him as filial and incorrupt; the province appointed him adjutant, senior clerk, and chief clerk, and nominated him for unusual conduct; the ducal offices summoned him five times as erudite, and he was twice imperially summoned, yet never took office.
translations.idiomatic: Filial-and-incorrupt nomination, provincial staff posts, special recommendation for outstanding virtue, five erudite summonses from the ministries, and two imperial calls—all went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 武惠時計吏至台，帝輒訪其安不。

translations.literal: During the reigns of Emperors Wu and Hui, when year-end accounting clerks reached the capital, the emperor always asked whether Miao was well.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tribute clerks from the provinces arrived at court under Emperors Wu and Hui, the sovereign inquired after Xu Miao’s health.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺命濯巾浣衣，榆棺雜磚，露車載屍，葦席瓦器而已。

translations.literal: When he died he left instructions for a rinsed headcloth and washed garments, an elm coffin with plain brick lining, a bare cart to bear the corpse, and nothing beyond reed mats and earthen vessels.
translations.idiomatic: His testament called for simple washed clothes, a humble elm coffin, an uncovered hearse, and only rush mats and pottery for grave goods.

sentences.zh: 崔遊

translations.literal: Cui You
translations.idiomatic: Cui You

sentences.zh: 崔遊，字子相，上黨人也。

translations.literal: Cui You, styled Zixiang, was a man of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui You, courtesy Zixiang, came from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 少好學，儒術甄明，恬靖謙退，自少及長，口未嘗語及財利。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; his Ru arts were discriminating and clear; he was quiet, peaceful, and modestly retiring; from childhood to adulthood his mouth never spoke of profit.
translations.idiomatic: He studied eagerly, mastered classical doctrine, lived in quiet humility, and never mentioned money.

sentences.zh: 魏末，察孝廉，除相府舍人，出為氐池長，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he was inspected as filial and incorrupt, appointed a retainer clerk in the minister’s office, and sent out as magistrate of Dichi, where his benevolent rule was conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wei he earned a filial-and-incorrupt nomination, served as a chancellery clerk, then governed Dichi county with a reputation for kindness.

sentences.zh: 以病免，遂為廢疾。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed and thereafter was considered chronically infirm.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him out of office, after which he was treated as permanently disabled.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，武帝祿敘文帝故府僚屬，就家拜郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, Emperor Wu, in ordering salaries for the former subordinates of Emperor Wen, went to his home and appointed him gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi, Emperor Wu granted stipends to Sima Zhao’s old staff and, calling at Cui You’s house, named him a palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，猶敦學不倦，撰《喪服圖》，行於世。

translations.literal: Past seventy he still pursued learning tirelessly and compiled Diagrams of Mourning Garments, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond seventy he kept studying without flagging and published Diagrams of Mourning Dress, which was widely read.

sentences.zh: 及劉元海僭位，命為御史大夫，固辭不就。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuan usurped the throne he ordered You to be grandee secretary; You firmly declined and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, having proclaimed himself ruler, named him censor-in-chief; Cui You steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，時年九十三。

translations.literal: He died at home at the age of ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 范隆

translations.literal: Fan Long
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long

sentences.zh: 范隆，字玄嵩，雁門人。

translations.literal: Fan Long, styled Xuansong, was a man of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long, courtesy Xuansong, was a native of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 父方，魏雁門太守。

translations.literal: His father Fang was governor of Yanmen for Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fang had governed Yanmen under Wei.

sentences.zh: 隆在孕十五月，生而父亡。

translations.literal: Long was in the womb fifteen months; he was born and his father died.
translations.idiomatic: He gestated fifteen months and was born only after his father had died.

sentences.zh: 年四歲，又喪母，哀號之聲，感慟行路。

translations.literal: At age four he again lost his mother; the sound of his wailing moved passersby to grief.
translations.idiomatic: At four he lost his mother as well, and his cries wrung tears from strangers on the road.

sentences.zh: 單孤無緦功之親，疏族范廣湣而養之，迎歸教書，為立祠堂。

translations.literal: Orphaned and alone, he lacked even distant relatives within the five grades of mourning; a collateral clansman Fan Guang pitied him and raised him, brought him home to teach him writing, and built an ancestral shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: With no kin even in the outer mourning grades, a cousin Fan Guang took pity, adopted him, taught him letters, and erected a lineage temple.

sentences.zh: 隆好學修謹，奉廣如父。

translations.literal: Long loved learning and cultivated careful conduct, serving Guang as he would a father.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long studied diligently and treated Fan Guang like a father.

sentences.zh: 博通經籍，無所不覽，著《春秋三傳》，撰《三禮吉凶宗紀》，甚有條義。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered the classics and omitted nothing in his reading; he authored the Three Traditions to the Spring and Autumn and compiled Auspicious and Inauspicious Ritual Summaries for the Three Rites, all very systematic in argument.
translations.idiomatic: He read every canonical text, wrote on the three Spring and Autumn commentaries, and produced ritual digests for the three Rites, each tightly reasoned.

sentences.zh: 惠帝時，天下將亂，隆隱跡不應州郡之命，晝勤耕稼，夜誦書典。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui, as the realm was about to fall into chaos, Long hid his traces and did not answer summons from province or commandery; by day he toiled in farming, by night he recited books.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui’s reign neared collapse, he vanished from public life, ignored every appointment, farmed by day, and read by night.

sentences.zh: 頗習秘曆陰陽之學，知并州將有氛祲之祥，故彌不復出仕。

translations.literal: He had studied secret calendars and yin-yang lore and knew that Bing province would show omens of military calamity, therefore he all the more refused office.
translations.idiomatic: His knowledge of astrology and portents told him Bingzhou would soon see war, so he doubled his resolve to stay out of government.

sentences.zh: 與上党朱紀友善，嘗共紀遊山，見一父老於窮澗之濱。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Zhu Ji of Shangdang; once he roamed a mountain with Ji and saw an old man beside a remote stream.
translations.idiomatic: He and his Shangdang friend Zhu Ji were hiking when they met an elder by a secluded brook.

sentences.zh: 父老曰：「二公何為在此？

translations.literal: The old man said, "What are you two gentlemen doing here?"
translations.idiomatic: The stranger asked, "What are you two gentlemen doing here?"

sentences.zh: 」隆等拜之，仰視則不見。

translations.literal: Long and the others bowed to him; when they looked up he was no longer visible.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed, but when they raised their eyes the figure had vanished.

sentences.zh: 後與紀依于劉元海，元海以隆為大鴻臚，紀為太常，並封公。

translations.literal: Later Long and Ji attached themselves to Liu Yuan; Yuan appointed Long grand herald and Ji minister of sacrifices, enfeoffing both as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Later both served Liu Yuan, who made Fan Long grand herald and Zhu Ji minister of sacrifices, each with a ducal fief.

sentences.zh: 隆死于劉聰之世，聰贈太師。

translations.literal: Long died under Liu Cong’s reign, and Cong posthumously honored him as grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long died during Liu Cong’s rule, and Liu Cong awarded him the posthumous title of grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 杜夷

translations.literal: Du Yi
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi

sentences.zh: 杜夷，字行齊，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: Du Yi, styled Xingqi, was a man of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi, courtesy Xingqi, came from Qian in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 世以儒學稱，為郡著姓。

translations.literal: For generations the family had been famed for Ru learning and was a prominent surname in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Du were known for classical scholarship and ranked among the commandery’s great clans.

sentences.zh: 夷少而恬泊，操尚貞素，居甚貧窘，不營產業，博覽經籍百家之書，算曆圖緯靡不畢究。

translations.literal: Yi from youth was tranquil and detached; his conduct prized chastity and simplicity; he lived in extreme want and did not build up property; he read broadly in the classics, masters, and hundred schools, omitting none of numerology, calendars, charts, or weft texts.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi was calm and austere from boyhood, spurned wealth, and devoured every branch of learning—classics, philosophers, mathematics, calendars, and apocrypha.

sentences.zh: 寓居汝潁之間，十載足不出門。

translations.literal: He lodged between the Ru and Ying rivers and for ten years did not step outside his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He lived between the Ru and Ying valleys and stayed indoors for a full decade.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，始還鄉里，閉門教授，生徒千人。

translations.literal: Past forty he returned to his home district, closed his door to teach, and had a thousand disciples.
translations.idiomatic: After forty he went home, taught behind closed doors, and drew a thousand students.

sentences.zh: 惠帝時三察孝廉，州命別駕，永嘉初，公車徵拜博士，太傅、東海王越辟，並不就。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui he was thrice inspected as filial and incorrupt; the province ordered him chief clerk; at the beginning of Yongjia the imperial carriage office summoned him as erudite, and the grand tutor, the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, summoned him—he accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui thrice nominated him filial and incorrupt, the province named him chief clerk, Yongjia brought an erudite summons, and Sima Yue called him to staff—he turned them all down.

sentences.zh: 懷帝詔王公舉賢良方正，刺史王敦以賀循為賢良，夷為方正，乃上疏曰：「臣聞有唐疇咨，元凱時登；

translations.literal: Emperor Huai ordered the princes and dukes to recommend worthy and upright men; the inspector Wang Dun nominated He Xun as worthy and Du Yi as upright, whereupon [Dun] submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that when Tang [Yao] made inquiry in the fields, the eight worthies timely ascended office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai asked nobles to recommend candid talent; Wang Dun put forward He Xun as worthy and Du Yi as incorrupt, then memorialized: "When sage-kings like Yao sought men in the countryside, the eight paragons rose to serve.

sentences.zh: 漢武欽賢，俊彥回應，故能允協時雍，敷崇盛化。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han revered worthies, and outstanding men responded; therefore he could harmonize the age and spread a flourishing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi’s respect for talent drew brilliant men to court, letting him align the times and extend a golden age of culture.

sentences.zh: 伏見太孫舍人會稽賀循、處士盧江杜夷履道彌高，清操絕俗，思學融通，才經王務。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that attendant to the heir’s son He Xun of Kuaiji and recluse Du Yi of Lujiang walk the Way ever higher, keep conduct pure beyond the vulgar, unite reflection and learning, and possess ability to manage royal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I see that He Xun, attendant to the imperial grandson, and Du Yi of Lujiang, though living as a commoner, pursue the highest virtue, shun worldliness, marry thought to erudition, and have the skill to govern.

sentences.zh: 循宰二縣，皆有名績，備僚東宮，忠恪允著。

translations.literal: Xun governed two counties, in each leaving a notable record; serving in the Eastern Palace, his loyalty and diligence were manifest.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun’s two county magistracies won praise, and his service in the heir’s residence showed conspicuous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 夷清虛沖淡，與俗異軌，考槃空谷，肥遁匿跡。

translations.literal: Yi is clear, empty, and calm, walking a path unlike the crowd; he tunes his lute in an empty valley, fat and hidden, erasing his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi lives in lucid detachment far from fashion, like the recluse of the Classic of Poetry, effacing himself in the hills.

sentences.zh: 蓋經國之良寶，聘命之所急。

translations.literal: They are indeed treasures for ordering the state and urgent targets for recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Such men are jewels for the realm and should be summoned without delay.

sentences.zh: 若得待詔公車，承對冊問，必有忠讜良謨，弘益政道矣。

translations.literal: If they may await edict at the carriage office and answer questions on the examination tablets, they will surely offer loyal counsel and excellent plans that broaden the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Let them present themselves at the capital examination hall; they will supply straight advice and sound strategy to improve policy.

sentences.zh: 」敦於是逼夷赴洛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dun forced Yi to go to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun then bullied Du Yi toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 夷遁于壽陽。

translations.literal: Yi fled to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi escaped to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍周馥，傾心禮接，引為參軍，夷辭之以疾。

translations.literal: The general who stabilizes the east, Zhou Fu, bowed to him with full courtesy and invited him as staff adviser; Yi declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, general who stabilizes the east, treated him with reverence and offered a staff post; Du Yi pleaded sickness.

sentences.zh: 馥知不可屈，乃自詣夷，為起宅宇，供其醫藥。

translations.literal: Fu knew he could not bend him, so went in person to Yi, built him a house, and supplied his medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not compel him, Zhou Fu visited him directly, erected a dwelling, and paid his medical bills.

sentences.zh: 馥敗，夷歸舊居，道遇兵寇。

translations.literal: When Fu was defeated, Yi returned to his old home and on the road encountered armed bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Fu’s fall Du Yi headed home and ran into raiders.

sentences.zh: 刺史劉陶告盧江郡曰：「昔魏文侯軾幹木之閭，齊相曹參尊崇蓋公，皆所以優賢表德，敦勵末俗。

translations.literal: Inspector Liu Tao informed Lujiang commandery: "Long ago Marquis Wen of Wei touched his carriage shafts before Duan Ganmu’s lane, and Chancellor Cao Shen of Qi honored Master Gai—all to honor worthies, display virtue, and encourage a jaded populace.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Liu Tao wrote Lujiang: "Wei Wenhou once slowed his chariot before Duan Ganmu’s lane, and Han Chancellor Cao Can revered Master Gai—both gestures meant to exalt the virtuous and shame a coarse age.

sentences.zh: 徵士杜君德懋行潔，高尚其志，頃流離道路，聞其頓躓，刺史忝任，不能崇飾有道，而使高操之士有此艱屯。

translations.literal: The summoned gentleman Du is of rich virtue and clean conduct, lofty in purpose; recently he has wandered the roads in exile, and I hear he has stumbled into hardship; this inspector, shamed by his charge, has failed to adorn the way of the worthy and has allowed a man of high principle to suffer such distress.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Du Yi bears weighty character and spotless honor, yet wanders destitute; I blush that I have not upheld the rites for recluses and have let a man of his stature fall into want.

sentences.zh: 今遣吏宣慰，郡可遣一吏，縣五吏，恆營恤之，常以市租供給家人糧廩，勿令闕乏。

translations.literal: Now I dispatch clerks to console him; the commandery shall send one clerk and each county five, to provide constant relief, regularly supplying his household with grain from market rents so they never lack.
translations.idiomatic: I am sending officers to comfort him: the commandery will detail one clerk and each county five, to sustain his family on market-tax grain without interruption.

sentences.zh: 」尋以胡寇，又移渡江，王導遣吏周贍之。

translations.literal: Soon, because of Hu raiders, he moved again across the Yangzi, and Wang Dao sent the clerk Zhou Shan to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raids soon drove him south of the river, where Wang Dao detailed Zhou Shan to help.

sentences.zh: 元帝為丞相，教曰：「今大義頹替，禮典無宗，朝廷滯義莫能攸正，宜特立儒林祭酒官，以弘其事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was minister of the left he instructed: "Now the great norm has crumbled and ritual canons lack a standard; the court’s unresolved doubts have no one to correct them; a special office of libationer for the Forest of Ru ought to be created to promote the matter.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Emperor Yuan ordered: "With moral order collapsed and ritual without anchor, someone must settle disputed precedents—establish a Forest-of-Ru libationer to lead the effort.

sentences.zh: 處士杜夷棲情遺遠，確然絕俗，才學精博，道行優備，其以夷為祭酒。

translations.literal: The recluse Du Yi harbors intentions far from the dust, stands resolutely apart from vulgar ways, combines refined learning with broad mastery, and excels in conduct as well as doctrine—let Yi be libationer.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman Du Yi, aloof from the world, learned and upright in equal measure, shall be named libationer."

sentences.zh: 」夷辭疾，未嘗朝會。

translations.literal: Yi pleaded illness and never attended court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi cited ill health and skipped every court session.

sentences.zh: 帝常欲詣夷，夷陳萬乘之主不宜往庶人之家。

translations.literal: The emperor often wished to visit Yi, but Yi declared that a ruler of ten thousand chariots ought not go to a commoner’s house.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign wished to call on him; Du Yi protested that an emperor should not darken a subject’s door.

sentences.zh: 帝乃與夷書曰：「吾與足下雖情在忘言，然虛心歷載。

translations.literal: The emperor then wrote Yi: "Between you and me, though feeling runs too deep for words, I have humbled my heart toward you for years.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler answered in a letter: "Though we need not speak to understand each other, I have long honored you in silence.

sentences.zh: 正以足下羸疾，故欲相省，甯論常儀也！

translations.literal: It is only because you are frail and ill that I wished to look in on you—why should we fuss over ordinary etiquette!"
translations.idiomatic: Precisely because you are weak and sick I mean to visit—surely stiff ceremony should not stand in the way!"

sentences.zh: 」又除國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed libationer of the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named libationer of the national university.

sentences.zh: 建武中，令曰：「國子祭酒杜夷安貧樂道，靜志衡門，日不暇給，雖原憲無以加也。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era an edict said: "The imperial-academy libationer Du Yi is content with poverty and devoted to the Way; his mind rests at his brushwood gate; his days admit no leisure—even Yuan Xian could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwu the court proclaimed: "Du Yi, libationer of the academy, embraces poverty for the sake of learning and keeps to his humble gate with never a free hour—not even Yuan Xian could outdo such devotion.

sentences.zh: 其賜穀二百斛。

translations.literal: Let him be granted two hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him two hundred hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 」皇太子三至夷第，執經問義。

translations.literal: The heir apparent thrice went to Yi’s residence, holding the classics to inquire into their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince visited Du Yi’s home three times, classic in hand, to discuss doctrine.

sentences.zh: 夷雖逼時命，亦未嘗朝謁，國有大政，恆就夷諮訪焉。

translations.literal: Although Yi was pressed by the mandates of the times, he still never presented himself at court for audience; when the state had great policies, they always went to Yi for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Though office nominally bound him, Du Yi never attended court; on weighty affairs the government still sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，夷自表請退。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Yi submitted a memorial of his own asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming’s accession brought Du Yi’s personal petition to step down.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先王之道將墜於地，君下帷研思，今之劉、楊。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The way of the former kings is about to fall to the ground; you, sir, let down the curtain and ponder—today’s Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "The sages’ teaching is failing; you study behind closed doors like a latter-day Liu Xiang or Yang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 搢紳之徒景仰軌訓，豈得高退，而朕靡所取則焉！

translations.literal: Gentry in sashes look up to your tracks and instructions—how can you retire to the heights while I lack a model to take!"
translations.idiomatic: Officials everywhere take you as their beacon—how can you withdraw and leave me without a standard?"

sentences.zh: 」太甯元年卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taining he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taining year one at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈大鴻臚，諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded grand herald and given the posthumous name Zhenzi, Master Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named him grand herald with the style Zhenzi.

sentences.zh: 夷臨終，遺命子晏曰：「吾少不出身，頃雖見羈錄，冠舄之飾，未嘗加體，其角巾素衣，斂以時服，殯葬之事，務從簡儉，亦不須苟取矯異也。

translations.literal: When Yi faced death he left instructions to his son Yan: "In youth I never entered office; though lately I have been bound to the register, the adornments of cap and shoes have never been placed on my body—use only a scholar’s kerchief and plain garments, enshroud me in everyday dress, and in burial rites strive for simplicity; there is likewise no need to affect eccentric austerity."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi’s deathbed words to Du Yan: "I shunned office in youth; even when later pressed into service I never truly wore court regalia—bury me in a plain cap and robe with timely, modest rites, neither lavish nor ostentatiously harsh."

sentences.zh: 」夷所著《幽求子》二十篇行於世。

translations.literal: Yi’s composition Seeking Stillness in Obscurity in twenty chapters circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His twenty-chapter Seeking Stillness in Obscurity circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 晏仕至蒼梧太守。

translations.literal: Yan rose in office to governor of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan became governor of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 夷兄弟三人。

translations.literal: Yi and his brothers were three in number.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yi was one of three brothers.

sentences.zh: 兄崧，字行高，亦有志節。

translations.literal: The elder brother Song, styled Xinggao, likewise possessed resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Du Song, courtesy Xinggao, showed the same moral fiber.

sentences.zh: 惠帝時，俗多浮偽，著《任子春秋》以刺之。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui, when custom was mostly hollow and hypocritical, he wrote the Spring and Autumn of Appointing Sons to satirize it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui’s court ran to vanity, Du Song composed the Spring and Autumn of Appointing Sons as a satire.

sentences.zh: 弟援，高平相。

translations.literal: The younger brother Yuan was chancellor of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Yuan served as chancellor of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 援子潛，右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yuan’s son Qian was general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan’s son Qian became general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 董景道

translations.literal: Dong Jingdao
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jingdao

sentences.zh: 董景道，字文博，弘農人也。

translations.literal: Dong Jingdao, styled Wenbo, was a man of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jingdao, courtesy Wenbo, hailed from Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 少而好學，千里追師，所在惟晝夜讀誦，略不與人交通。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, traveling a thousand li to pursue a teacher; wherever he was he read and recited day and night, scarcely interacting with others.
translations.idiomatic: He studied fanatically, crossing great distances to find masters, and buried himself in texts night and day with little social contact.

sentences.zh: 明《春秋三傳》、《京氏易》、《馬氏尚書》、《韓詩》，皆精究大義。

translations.literal: He clarified the three traditions to the Spring and Autumn, the Changes of the Jing family, the Documents of the Ma family, and the Han Poetry, in each case penetrating the great meanings.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the three Spring and Autumn commentaries, Jing Fang’s Changes, the Ma family Documents, and the Han version of the Poetry down to their core arguments.

sentences.zh: 《三禮》之義，專遵鄭氏，著《禮通論》非駁諸儒，演廣鄭旨。

translations.literal: As for the meanings of the Three Rites, he followed Zheng Xuan exclusively; he authored Comprehensive Discourse on the Rites, not to refute the various Ru but to expand Zheng’s intentions.
translations.idiomatic: On the three ritual classics he stood with Zheng Xuan, writing Comprehensive Discourse on the Rites to elaborate Zheng rather than attack other schools.

sentences.zh: 永平中，知天下將亂，隱於商洛山，衣木葉，食樹果，彈琴歌笑以自娛，毒蟲猛獸皆繞其傍，是以劉元海及聰屢征，皆礙而不達。

translations.literal: In the Yongping years, knowing the realm would fall into chaos, he hid on Mount Shangluo, clothed himself in tree leaves, fed on tree fruits, and amused himself by strumming a zither, singing, and laughing; poisonous insects and fierce beasts all circled about him, so that Liu Yuan and Cong repeatedly summoned him but were always obstructed and could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era he foresaw collapse, fled to Mount Shangluo, dressed in leaves, lived on wild fruit, and passed time with lute and song; venomous creatures and beasts haunted his hut, so Liu Yuan and Liu Cong’s repeated summons never got through.

sentences.zh: 至劉曜時出山，廬於渭汭。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao held power he left the mountain and built a hut on the bend of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Yao he emerged and dwelt by the Wei’s shore.

sentences.zh: 曜徵為太子少傅、散騎常侍，並固辭，竟以壽終。

translations.literal: Yao summoned him as junior tutor to the heir apparent and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; he firmly declined both, and in the end died at his natural span.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao offered him tutor to the crown prince and cavalier attendant; he refused steadfastly and died in peace.

sentences.zh: 續咸

translations.literal: Xu Xian
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xian

sentences.zh: 續咸，字孝宗，上黨人也。

translations.literal: Xu Xian, styled Xiaozong, was a man of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xian, courtesy Xiaozong, came from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 性孝謹敦重，履道貞素。

translations.literal: By nature he was filial, careful, earnest, and weighty; he trod the Way with chaste simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He was dutiful, grave, and lived plainly by principle.

sentences.zh: 好學，師事京兆杜預，專《春秋》、《鄭氏易》、教授常數十人，博覽群言，高才善文論。

translations.literal: He loved learning, studied under Du Yu of Jingzhao, specialized in the Spring and Autumn and Zheng’s Changes, regularly had several tens of pupils, read widely among writers, and with high talent was skilled in essays and disquisitions.
translations.idiomatic: A student of Du Yu, he taught dozens of disciples, focused on the Spring and Autumn and Zheng’s Changes, read omnivorously, and wrote brilliant essays.

sentences.zh: 又修陳杜律，明達刑書。

translations.literal: He also revised the Chen–Du statutes and was lucid in penal writings.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the legal codes associated with Chen and Du and knew criminal law inside out.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，曆廷尉平、東安太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia years he served in turn as assistant in the court of trials and governor of Dong’an.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia he rose to assistant magistrate of the supreme court and governor of Dong’an.

sentences.zh: 劉琨承制於并州，以為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Liu Kun, exercising discretionary authority in Bingzhou, appointed him staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun, ruling Bingzhou on emergency authority, named him staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 後遂沒石勒，勒以為理曹參軍。

translations.literal: Afterward he fell captive to Shi Le, and Le made him adjutant in the bureau of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Captured by Shi Le, he became an adjutant in the legal section of Shi’s regime.

sentences.zh: 持法平詳，當時稱其清裕，比之於公。

translations.literal: He held the law even and thorough; people of the time praised his clarity and ease, comparing him to the impartial lord [Yu Gong].
translations.idiomatic: His judgments were balanced and meticulous; contemporaries likened his fairness to the legendary upright judge.

sentences.zh: 著《遠遊志》、《異物志》、《汲塚古文釋》皆十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Records of Far Roaming, Records of Strange Things, and Exegesis of the Ancient Text from the Ji Tomb, each ten fascicles, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of Far Roaming, Records of Strange Things, and Exegesis of the Ji Tomb Texts—ten scrolls each—all of which circulated.

sentences.zh: 年九十七，死于石季龍之世，季龍贈儀同三司。

translations.literal: At ninety-seven he died in the era of Shi Jilong, and Jilong posthumously awarded him the three offices of equal ceremonial rank.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-seven under Shi Hu, who posthumously granted him the honorific "three offices of equal rank" to the throne.

sentences.zh: 徐邈

translations.literal: Xu Miao
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao

sentences.zh: 徐邈，東莞姑幕人也。

translations.literal: Xu Miao was a man of Gumu in Dongguan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao came from Gumu in Dongguan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖澄之為州治中，屬永嘉之亂，遂與鄉人臧琨等率子弟並閭里士庶千餘家，南渡江，家於京口。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng had been senior clerk in the province; when the Yongjia disorders struck, he together with his townsman Zang Kun and others led more than a thousand families of kinsmen, neighbors, gentry, and commoners south across the Yangzi and settled at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served as provincial chief clerk; at the Yongjia upheaval he joined Zang Kun and others in shepherding over a thousand households of kin and neighbors south to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 父藻，都水使者。

translations.literal: His father Zao was commissioner of waterways.
